(120132) 2003 FY
128
(
provisional designation
2003 FY
128
) is a
trans-Neptunian object
with a diameter of about 460 km.
[
3
]
It orbits the
Sun
at a distance of about 49.81
astronomical units
.
[
2
]
It was discovered on 26 March 2003 by the
NEAT
program at the
Palomar Observatory
,
California
.
Orbital Classification
It is classified as a
detached object
by the
Deep Ecliptic Survey
(DES), since its orbit appears to be beyond the current control of
Neptune
.
[
1
]
Though, if Neptune
migrated outward
, there would have been a period when Neptune had a higher eccentricity.
